statement_en: The dimension of a graph $G$ is the minimal $n$ such that $G$ can be embedded in $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that every edge of $G$ is a unit line segment. What is the smallest number of edges in a graph with dimension $4$?
statement_lean:
namespace SimpleGraph
open Finset List
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
def UnitDistanceEmbeddable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℝ^n, Function.Injective f ∧ ∀ u v : V, G.Adj u v → dist (f u) (f v) = 1
end SimpleGraph

namespace SimpleGraph
open Finset List
open scoped EuclideanGeometry
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
def HasDimension {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsLeast {m | UnitDistanceEmbeddable G m} n
end SimpleGraph

open scoped EuclideanGeometry
variable {V : Type*}

theorem erdos_50714 :
    IsLeast {m | ∃ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.HasDimension 4 ∧ G.edgeSet.ncard = m}
      9 := by
  sorry
